title: Pre-Market Briefing - 2026-08-10
markdown:
# Pre-Market Briefing

## 1. Market Tone
- **Confirmed:** Friday’s market was risk-on: **S&P 500** +0.62%, **Nasdaq** +1.3%, **Dow** +0.28%, **Bitcoin** +0.81% (Motley Fool).
- **Confirmed:** The prior week was strong, with the S&P 500 up 3.58% to a record and the Nasdaq up 5.19% (Motley Fool).
- **Interpretation:** Tone entering the open looks constructive but potentially pause-prone, with futures described as “quieter” and only modestly higher (Motley Fool).

## 2. Macro And Calendar
- **Confirmed:** The weak July jobs report is still driving expectations for Fed cuts (Motley Fool).
- **Confirmed:** Wednesday’s July CPI is the key macro test; consensus cited at **3.4% YoY headline** and **2.5% core** (Motley Fool).
- **Why it matters:** A cooler CPI could reinforce September cut odds; a hotter CPI could unwind some of Friday’s optimism (Motley Fool).
- **Open question:** No other macro events or economic releases were provided in the source.

## 3. Earnings And Company News
- **Berkshire Hathaway (**BRK.A/BRK.B**)**: Operating earnings up 16% YoY; insurance was rough, but energy and manufacturing/services/retail were strong. Cash fell to **$365.5B** from **$397.4B** as Berkshire bought back stock, closed Taylor Morrison, and became a net buyer of stocks for the first time in more than three years. Stock was little-changed pre-market (Motley Fool).
- **Cellebrite (**CLBT**)**: Reports Thursday before the bell. The article says the key test is whether new business reaccelerates after a slow Q1, especially federal and European sales, margins, and actual AI-product revenue (Motley Fool).
- **Cisco (**CSCO**)**: Reports Wednesday after the close. Street expects about **$1.17 EPS** on **$16.82B revenue**. AI infrastructure orders and Silicon One demand are the focus; guidance matters more than the beat because valuation is already stretched (Motley Fool).
- **Rocket Lab (**RKLB**)**: Reports after today’s close. Management expects **$225M–$240M revenue** and **38%–40% non-GAAP gross margin**. Watch Neutron, Mynaric integration, and the pending Motiv Space Systems deal (Motley Fool).
- **On Holding (**ONON**)**: Reports before tomorrow’s open. Consensus is near **$0.41 EPS** on roughly **$1.1B revenue**. Constant-currency growth and durable margins are the focus; implied move is about 8% (Motley Fool).
- **BBB Foods (**TBBB**)**: Reports after Wednesday’s close. Consensus is revenue up about 47% with a wider loss; the question is whether losses are mostly non-cash stock comp or real operating weakness (Motley Fool).
- **CAVA (**CAVA**)**: Reports after Tuesday’s close. Consensus is **$360.1M revenue** and **$0.18 EPS**. Same-restaurant sales and margin resilience matter more than the salmon-launch margin pressure (Motley Fool).
- **DoorDash (**DASH**)**: Article is long-term positive but does not provide a new near-term catalyst in this email. It notes drone regulatory clearance, 970 million orders last quarter, and $1.4B quarterly free cash flow (Motley Fool).

## 4. Top Movers And Catalysts
- **Confirmed:** No explicit pre-market gap movers or live price movers were provided.
- **Potentially relevant catalysts into/after the open:**
  - **BRK.B**: Q2 results and first net stock buying in over three years.
  - **RKLB**: After-close earnings today.
  - **ONON**: Before-open earnings tomorrow.
  - **CAVA**: After-close earnings Tuesday.
  - **CSCO**: After-close earnings Wednesday.
  - **TBBB**: After-close earnings Wednesday.
  - **CLBT**: Before-open earnings Thursday.

## 5. Ranked Buy Candidates
> These are not forced buys; they are simply the strongest swingable ideas from the source material.

### 1) **BRK.B** — Catalyst Continuation
- **Catalyst:** Berkshire’s operating earnings rose 16%, and the bigger story is cash deployment after years of inactivity: buybacks, acquisition completion, and net stock buying for the first time in more than three years (Motley Fool).
- **Why it might matter for a swing trade:** The market often responds to a shift from capital hoarding to capital deployment, especially when backed by strong operating results.
- **What would invalidate it:** If the market decides the stock purchases were small, non-strategic, or if the insurance weakness dominates the read-through.
- **What must be checked before entry:** Pre-market price reaction, whether the earnings release supports the article’s “little-changed” tone, and whether the Q2 filing/13-F later confirms meaningful purchases.
- **Pass if:** Price is already extended or the move is fading without follow-through.

### 2) **RKLB** — Catalyst Continuation
- **Catalyst:** After-close Q2 results are expected to show record revenue of **$225M–$240M** and **38%–40% gross margin** (management guidance cited by Motley Fool).
- **Why it might matter for a swing trade:** A company with record revenue plus a visible pipeline can trade well if execution and guidance support the growth story.
- **What would invalidate it:** Revenue below guidance, weaker-than-expected margins, or concerns that spending discipline is slipping.
- **What must be checked before entry:** The actual print vs. guided range, commentary on Neutron, Mynaric, and Motiv, and any sign of dilution/accelerating losses.
- **Pass if:** The report is “good enough” but guidance is soft or the stock gaps too far beyond a clean risk point.

### 3) **ONON** — Reversal Bounce / Catalyst Continuation
- **Catalyst:** Earnings before tomorrow’s open; focus is on constant-currency growth and margins, not the strong franc noise (Motley Fool).
- **Why it might matter for a swing trade:** If the company proves premium pricing power and margins hold, the market may reward it despite valuation concerns.
- **What would invalidate it:** Slowing constant-currency growth, margin pressure, or cautious guidance.
- **What must be checked before entry:** Pre-open reaction to results, whether guidance offsets valuation concerns, and whether the implied 8% move creates a tradable overreaction.
- **Pass if:** The stock is too expensive to chase into the report or the numbers are merely in-line.

### 4) **CAVA** — Catalyst Continuation
- **Catalyst:** Tuesday after-close earnings with expectations of **$360.1M revenue** and **$0.18 EPS**; same-restaurant sales are the key tell (Motley Fool).
- **Why it might matter for a swing trade:** If same-store sales stay strong, margin pressure from salmon launch costs may be absorbed as part of growth execution.
- **What would invalidate it:** Softer same-restaurant sales or margin pressure that looks worse than the expected roughly 1-point hit.
- **What must be checked before entry:** Same-restaurant sales trend, margin commentary, and whether newer growth initiatives are actually scaling.
- **Pass if:** Sales comp is weak or the reaction depends solely on hope around long-term initiatives.

## 6. Swing Setup Board
| Ticker | Classification | Setup | Trigger | Stop / Invalidation | First Target Logic | Sizing Caution | Pass If |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **BRK.B** | Trend Pullback / Catalyst Continuation | Post-earnings cash deployment story | Holds firm after earnings and reclaims/holds opening range strength | Weak reaction or continued drift lower despite the earnings beat | Test recent highs / prior reaction zone if momentum builds | Moderate size; market may treat cash deployment as slow-burn, not immediate upside | No follow-through or the market focuses only on insurance weakness |
| **RKLB** | Breakout / Momentum | After-close earnings could create a strong gap setup | Gap-and-hold above the post-print high | Failure to hold the gap or loss of opening range low | Prior swing high or measured move from the earnings gap | Keep size smaller because post-earnings volatility is likely | Gap is too extended or guidance is merely adequate |
| **ONON** | Reversal Bounce | Implied 8% move creates room for an earnings reaction trade | Strong pre-open reaction and hold of first-hour support | Break below reaction low / failed gap hold | Fill gap toward first resistance / prior range highs | Reduce size; rich valuation means fast reversals are possible | Guidance disappoints or the move is already fully priced |
| **CAVA** | Catalyst Continuation | Earnings into same-store-sales check | If the print confirms healthy comps, watch for continuation | Weak comps or margin miss beyond expected pressure | Prior range high / earnings gap extension | Smaller size; food names can whipsaw on guidance | Sales comp softness overwhelms the story |

## 7. Setup Watch
- **CLBT** — Before-bell Thursday. Watch for reacceleration in federal/European sales and any real AI revenue mention (Motley Fool).
- **CSCO** — Wednesday after close. Watch AI infrastructure orders and Silicon One traction; guidance is key (Motley Fool).
- **TBBB** — Wednesday after close. Watch whether the wider loss is mostly stock comp or real operating weakness (Motley Fool).

## 8. Risk Watch
- **CPI risk:** Wednesday inflation data could reverse the rate-cut narrative if hotter than expected (Motley Fool).
- **Valuation risk:** **ONON** and **CSCO** are both flagged as names where guidance matters more because valuation is already stretched or meaningful (Motley Fool).
- **Execution risk:** **RKLB** needs Neutron progress, acquisition integration, and discipline to remain credible (Motley Fool).
- **Margin/comps risk:** **CAVA** needs same-store sales to hold up if salmon and labor pressure margins (Motley Fool).
- **Open question:** No explicit sector rotation data or breadth figures were provided beyond the strong week in semis.

## 9. Sector And Theme Watch
- **Semiconductors:** Strong rebound last week; iShares Semiconductor ETF rose 7.6% (Motley Fool).
- **Rate-cut narrative:** Weak jobs data boosted hopes for easier money, which continues to underpin equities (Motley Fool).
- **Consumer premium / growth quality:** **ONON** and **CAVA** both hinge on whether premium demand holds up under valuation and margin pressure (Motley Fool).
- **Space / defense-tech execution:** **RKLB** is a near-term catalyst name around commercialization and M&A integration (Motley Fool).
- **Capital deployment / conglomerate signal:** Berkshire’s move from hoarding to buying may support the “cash is finally working” theme (Motley Fool).

## 10. Worth Reading
- Berkshire’s Q2 results and cash deployment shift (Motley Fool).
- The CPI setup and why it matters more than the prior week’s rally (Motley Fool).
- Rocket Lab, On Holding, BBB Foods, and CAVA previews for near-term earnings context (Motley Fool).
- The DoorDash long-term conviction note, mainly as background on management-backed spending (Motley Fool).

## 11. Open Questions
- Will Berkshire’s stock buying turn into a larger, durable capital deployment change, or is it just a one-quarter event? (Motley Fool)
- Can **RKLB** hit the guided revenue/margin range and still provide enough forward clarity to support the stock?
- Does **ONON** show enough constant-currency growth to justify premium valuation?
- Will **CAVA** keep same-store sales strong enough to absorb the salmon-launch margin hit?
- Is **CSCO** getting real AI infrastructure demand, or just incremental noise?
- Is **TBBB**’s wider loss mostly non-cash stock compensation, or does it signal operating friction?

## Notable Noise
- **DASH** was discussed only in a long-term promotional context; no fresh near-term trading catalyst was provided.
- Berkshire’s total EPS more than doubled, but the email itself says that figure is mostly mark-to-market noise.
- No live pre-market price data or unusual volume leaders were provided for direct momentum trading.
